title: Enterprise onboarding — support process, health checks, QBR & escalation playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures used by Customer Success and Support when onboarding enterprise customers to Redwood Inference. It covers the end-to-end support process, integration handoff, escalation procedures, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. The document is intended as the canonical reference for customer-facing teams and engineering partners during the first 90 days and ongoing account cadence.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers through a deterministic onboarding process.
- Ensure rapid, consistent incident response with clear owners and SLAs.
- Establish a repeatable health-check and QBR cadence to surface risk and optimization opportunities.
- Provide integration runbooks, common troubleshooting steps, and known issue workarounds.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private deployment customers, and larger Hosted API customers with >$5k/mo usage or enterprise contracts.
- Covers pre-sales handoff, week-0 kickoff, week-1 integration, day-30 stabilization, and ongoing QBR cadence.

Roles & Ownership:
- Customer Success (CS) — Primary relationship manager, onboarding lead, QBR owner.
- Support (Tier 1) — First-line triage for customer issues, logs KIs, routes engineering escalations.
- Solutions Engineering (SE) — Integration lead, architecture signoff, assist with performance tuning.
- Eng-SRE — Incident response, SLO guardrails, production troubleshooting.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime — Deep model/runtime issues, kernel-level performance debugging.

Contact and Escalation Matrix (short):
1. Tier 1 Support (CS/Support team): support@redwood.example.com — business hours response.
2. SE Slack channel: #se-enterprise-onboard — used for technical clarifications during integration.
3. Eng-SRE Pager: pager duty (on-call) — P1/P0 incidents only.
4. Executive escalation: customer-success-leads@redwood.example.com — for SLA or contractual breaches.

Service Levels (example thresholds):
| Priority | Definition | Initial response | Target resolution (guideline) | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P0 | Production outage or critical data loss | 15 minutes | 4 hours | Eng-SRE (with SE & Serving Runtime) |
| P1 | Severe degradation, customer blocking | 1 hour | 1 business day | Eng-SRE & SE |
| P2 | Functional impact, workaround exists | 4 hours | 3 business days | Support / SE |
| P3 | Minor issues, feature requests | 1 business day | Next release / backlog | CS / Product |

Onboarding checklist (90-day plan):
1. Pre-kickoff (pre-PO / contract):
   - Validate contract & required compliance (data residency, KMS).
   - Create customer workspace in Console, enable access (RBAC) for SE and CS.
   - Assign onboarding owners and set calendar invites (Kickoff + weekly syncs).
2. Week 0 (Kickoff):
   - Kickoff agenda: goals, success metrics, integration plan, contacts, escalation matrix.
   - Share integration guide and sample code.
   - Security & network checklist: IP allowlists, VPC peering, egress rules.
3. Week 1 (Integration and Validation):
   - SE performs initial connectivity test, token provisioning, and sample inference runs.
   - Run the perf baseline: 1000 sample requests with representative prompts (SE provides script).
   - Validate model selection and quantization profile (if Dedicated/Private).
4. Day 14 (Stabilize):
   - Address integration defects, apply known workarounds if applicable, finalize SLOs.
   - Enable production observability: per-route dashboards, tracing, and error budgets.
5. Day 30 (Optimization):
   - Apply batching, caching and quantization recommendations. Measure cost/token impact.
   - Hand off operations runbook to customer (if Private) or CS for hosted customers.
6. Day 60–90 (QBR prep & handoff to CS):
   - Prepare first health review and QBR: uptime, latency percentiles, token usage, cost savings.
   - Define next-phase success metrics and optimization roadmap.

Integration guide (summary):
- Authentication: use Customer API key scoped to project. For Private deployments, exchange service account token via SAML/OAuth flow described in the Private Deployment on-boarding guide.
- Sample curl for ping and inference:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1", "input":"Hello" }'

- Network requirements:
  - Outbound HTTPS (443) to api.redwood.example.com and metrics.redwood.example.com.
  - For Dedicated/Private: allow connections to dedicated pool IPs provided during provisioning.

- Observability integration:
  - Provide customer with the per-route dashboard template (Grafana JSON) and OpenTelemetry export sample (collector config snippet).
  - Enable log-forwarding to customer SIEM (S3/Kinesis/Splunk) as contractually agreed.

Escalation playbook (step-by-step):
1. Triage (Support Tier 1):
   - Confirm customer identity, gather request id, timestamps, environment.
   - Reproduce the issue with the same inputs. Capture logs and trace IDs.
   - If P0/P1, escalate to Eng-SRE immediately and notify SE.
2. Engineering investigation (Eng-SRE + Serving Runtime):
   - Attach trace, logs, and perf profile. Check KV cache, batching logs, and GPU memory graphs.
   - Run perf debug tooling: /opt/redwood/bin/perf-check --trace <trace-id> (internal).
   - If root cause is a model issue, engage Applied ML/model-onboarding team.
3. Communication and updates:
   - Provide customer updates every 30 minutes for P0, hourly for P1.
   - CS owns external comms cadence and postmortem distribution.
4. Post-incident:
   - Complete incident review within 3 business days. Deliver RCA within 7 business days for P0s.

Known issues & common workarounds (living table):
| Symptom | Likely cause | Workaround | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intermittent 502s on generate endpoint | Upstream pod OOM during spike | Increase pod memory or enable throttled batching; enable fallback model route | Eng-Serving-Runtime |
| Large request latency spikes >99p | KV cache miss due to long prefix | Configure prefix caching TTL = 1h for repeated prompts; enable warm-up requests | SE |
| Tokenization mismatch between client & model | Old tokenizer bundle cached on client | Update client SDK to latest bundle; clear local tokenizer cache | Eng-DevEx |
| Embeddings similarity drift after model upgrade | New embedding vector space | Create migration mapping or re-index embeddings; rollback to previous model if needed | Applied ML |

Support process templates & artifacts:
- Week 1 perf-run script: perf/run_default_load_test.sh (SE will copy to customer workspace).
- QBR slide template: assets/qbr_template.pptx (use for month-1 and quarterly reviews).
- Postmortem template: templates/postmortem_template.md

Health checks and QBR cadence:
- Weekly health checks (automated): run daily synthetic checks for inference endpoint (5m cadence); check 50th/95th/99th latency and error rate >= 99.9% success.
- Monthly health summary (CS+SE): uptime, latency trends, token usage delta, cost per 1M tokens, model/regression alerts.
- Quarterly business review (QBR) agenda:
  1. Executive summary: adoption, ROI, open risks.
  2. Operational health: uptime, SLO attainment, incident summary.
  3. Cost & efficiency: cost/token, batching gains, recommended quantization.
  4. Product roadmap: upcoming features and deprecations.
  5. Action items and owners.

QBR deliverables:
- 30/60/90 day QBR decks for initial phase.
- Quarterly deck with operational metrics + recommendations.
- Follow-up action tracker (owner + due date) in customer workspace.

Reporting & dashboards (how to use):
- Primary dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token breakdown by model, error code distribution.
- Alert thresholds (recommended): p99 latency > 2s for >5 minutes, error rate > 0.5% for >10m.
- Cost alerts: daily token spend > 20% above forecast for 3 consecutive days.

Appendices:
A. Example incident communication template (P0) — subject: "[P0] Customer <X> inference outage — initial update".
B. Private deployment checklist: networking, KMS config, storage encryption, air-gap steps.
C. Useful commands (internal):
   - Check runtime health: curl -s http://runtime-host:9100/healthz
   - Dump current batching stats: /opt/redwood/bin/batch-stats --json > /tmp/batch-stats.json
